plan.why: the realized per-opponent caps differ — arm 40/39/1, control 8/12/3 (traced W/L/D per opponent, counted on disk); arm cut to 8/12/1

arm.population: LIVE cycle: 12 opponents (9 scripted bots + 3 pool sentinels) x 100 games, traced under the per-opponent OUTCOME QUOTA (loss-enriched, not a random subsample)

manifest.selection_rule: per-opponent per-cycle OUTCOME QUOTA: the first 40 losses, the first 10 DRAWS (a tie, or a 250-turn timeout — its OWN bucket, so a stall storm cannot evict the decisive losses), and the first 40 wins of each opponent are persisted as traces; every later battle is played (and counts toward the win rate) but is NOT traced. Under battle-level work-stealing each shard unit carries max(1, ceil(quota / n_shards)), so the per-opponent totals are approximately these. LOSS-ENRICHED BY DESIGN — the traces are a loss-forensics sample, never a random subsample of the cycle.

anchor.note: the anchor (label-trust) arm is a CENSUS of the bot battles it draws from and its estimand is the REPLAY DRIVER's fidelity, not a property of the eval population — capture-rate reweighting does NOT apply to it and none is applied.

dropped.random: the quota captured only one outcome class (40 wins of 40 battles) — nothing to reweight

frame.recorded_v_note: every conditioning row is computed on ONE eval cycle from the `win_probs` the trace npz RECORDED, which within a cycle IS that cycle's own model — no model forward is done. Pooling a recorded V across cycles would import the trainee's own improvement as between-opponent spread (head-refit hazard 3: CTRL reads 1.079 pooled against 0.066 frozen); this module never pools cycles.

strength.note: bot anchors + an ALL-STEPS bot-anchored refit of the run's snapshot ladder (4 nodes rated, anchored_to_bots=true), the positional sentinel map verified against the manifest's own win counts
